 The Reds find themselves trailing their upcoming visitors by four points ahead of Sunday’s duel. Ewan Ross-Murray | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source Liverpool have won their last four Anfield showdowns with Brighton. | Kristian Skeie/UEFA/Getty Images (Liverpool), Visionhaus/Getty Images (Brighton) Two of England’s form sides go head-to-head when Liverpool host Brighton & Hove Albion in the Premier League on Sunday. 
--> Two of England’s form sides go head-to-head when Liverpool host Brighton & Hove Albion in the Premier League on Sunday. 
 Both clubs have triumphed in four of their last five matches across all competitions, but it’s the Seagulls who somewhat surprisingly lead their upcoming hosts in the Premier League. An exceptional start to the campaign has yielded 16 points and an impressive 3–0 win over defending champions Arsenal, while the Reds have only picked up 12 points from their seven outings. 
--> Both clubs have triumphed in four of their last five matches across all competitions, but it’s the Seagulls who somewhat surprisingly lead their upcoming hosts in the Premier League. An exceptional start to the campaign has yielded 16 points and an impressive 3–0 win over defending champions Arsenal, while the Reds have only picked up 12 points from their seven outings. 
 Liverpool ’s recent triumphs have been laced with imperfections, however, largely stemming from the defense. They have conceded three times to LASK and Villarreal in their last two European outings, while also benefitting from a numerical advantage in their comeback victory over Brentford last weekend. 
--> Liverpool ’s recent triumphs have been laced with imperfections, however, largely stemming from the defense. They have conceded three times to LASK and Villarreal in their last two European outings, while also benefitting from a numerical advantage in their comeback victory over Brentford last weekend. 
 Brighton have been much more convincing, despite their goalless draw with Czech side Jablonec in the Conference League on Thursday. The 5–0 thrashing of rivals Crystal Palace last Sunday marked a sixth successive victory in all competitions, during which time they scored 22 times and conceded just twice.

 While Brighton’s defense has been impressively watertight—they’re currently on a run of five successive clean sheets—Liverpool have been less organized, as evidenced by them conceding three goals in three of their last four matches.

 Both managers demand high-intensity, attack-first soccer, hopefully resulting in an end-to-end and frenetic contest. Which way will it go? Only time will tell. 
--> Both managers demand high-intensity, attack-first soccer, hopefully resulting in an end-to-end and frenetic contest. Which way will it go? Only time will tell. 
 Head-to-head record : Brighton have lost their last four visits to Anfield, but interspersed have been victories on home soil during three of the last four campaigns. The Seagulls have caused issues for Liverpool since their Premier League arrival, although current momentum is with the weekend’s hosts. 
 Liverpool’s Anfield struggles : The Reds are without a Premier League win on home soil for six months, and could start the season without victory in any of their first four league matches for only the fourth time in their history.
 Brighton’s attacking stars : Fabian Hürzeler’s men journey north brimming with belief, especially in the final third. Pascal Groß has been the architect of their success so far with seven goal involvements in the league, but he’s been closely supported by the likes of Charalampos Kostoulas (5) and Maxim De Cuyper (4).
